# Chapter 9: Common Design Patterns — 9.3

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 9.3 Dependency Properties

- **FDG9051** DO provide properties as dependency properties if you need the properties to support WPF features such as styling, triggers, data binding, animations, dynamic resources, and inheritance. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9051

## 9.3.1 Dependency Property Design

- **FDG9052** DO inherit from `DependencyObject`, or one of its subtypes, when implementing dependency properties. The type provides a very efficient implementation of a property store and automatically supports WPF data binding. (partly checked) (not in test projects)
- **FDG9053** DO provide a regular CLR property and public static read-only field storing an instance of `System.Windows.DependencyProperty` for each dependency property. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9053
- **FDG9054** DO implement dependency properties by calling instance methods `DependencyObject.GetValue` and `DependencyObject.SetValue`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9054
- **FDG9055** DO name the dependency property static field by suffixing the name of the property with “Property.” (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9055
- **FDG9056** DO NOT set default values of dependency properties explicitly in code; instead, set them in metadata. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9056
- **FDG9057** DO NOT put code in the property accessors other than the standard code to access the static field. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9057
- **FDG9058** DO NOT use dependency properties to store secure data. Even private dependency properties can be accessed publicly. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9058

## 9.3.3 Dependency Property Validation

- **FDG9059** DO NOT put dependency property validation logic in the property’s accessors. Instead, pass a validation callback to `DependencyProperty.Register` method. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9059

## 9.3.4 Dependency Property Change Notifications

- **FDG9060** DO NOT implement change notification logic in dependency property accessors. Dependency properties have a built-in change notifications feature that is used by supplying a change notification callback to the `PropertyMetadata`. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9060

## 9.3.5 Dependency Property Value Coercion

- **FDG9061** DO NOT implement coercion logic in dependency property accessors. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch09-patterns-dependency-properties.md#fdg9061
